summary: Completes mymatasan's built-in user manual: the article set grows from the 6-article phase-1 launch set to 36 articles per language (144 files across en/ms/zh/ar), covering daily use (dashboard, live views, notifications, recordings, object search, people), cameras (adding cameras, camera properties, camera health, ONVIF management), detection (how detection works, detection rules, object classes, teach mode, fire/smoke/plate recognition, training models), recording (configuration, storage and capacity), notification destinations, administration (users and roles, settings reference, encryption at rest, backup and restore, updates and restart, secure wipe and reset, control plane, machine health), and an appendix (troubleshooting, FAQ, glossary). Contextual '?' help buttons (@shared/Manual's HelpButton) are now wired throughout the SPA at the point of use -- every Settings tab, every camera settings tab, the AI detection rules header, the People page and its consent gate, the Recordings header, Object Search, the dashboard anomaly panel, and Notifications -- each deep-linking to the specific manual section that explains it, instead of only the generic workspace-header help from phase 1. A new conformance guard, domain/shared/manual/manualcheck.UIReferences (exercised by apps/mymatasan/manual/manual_test.go's new TestManualUIReferences, currently 42 targets), scans the frontend source for every declared help target and fails the build if a button names an article slug or heading anchor that does not actually exist in the shipped manual -- catching the renamed-article/dropped-anchor class of bug that otherwise breaks a deep link silently (no compile or runtime error, the button just opens the wrong page).
compatibility: Backward compatible, additive only. No new HTTP routes, config keys, or schema changes -- the existing GET /api/manual endpoints and public/unauthenticated posture from phase 1 are unchanged. New articles and help buttons appear automatically on upgrade with no migration or config step; existing bookmarks/deep links into the phase-1 six articles keep working since none were renamed.
